newsitem.title: UK: N. Irish police arrest man over IRA bomb attack.
newsitem.headline: N. Irish police arrest man over IRA bomb attack.

text.p: Police investigating a double IRA bombing at Britain's army headquarters in Northern Ireland said on Thursday they had arrested a man.
Monday's assault at Lisburn, 10 miles (15 km) from Belfast was the guerrilla group's first attack in Northern Ireland for two years. Police called it "a deliberate attempt at mass murder".
"Early this morning, a male from the Belfast area was arrested," a police spokesman said. The man was being questioned.
He was detained under Britain's Prevention of Terrorism Act, which means he can be held for up to seven days before police have to either charge or release him.
The arrest came less than 24 hours after police issued a photofit picture of one of the suspected bombers, apparently heavily disguised in a hood, beard and dark glasses.
The IRA (Irish Republican Army), fighting to end British rule in Northern Ireland, has admitted to setting off two car bombs, each with 500 pounds (225 kg) of explosives, inside the army base.

Police said the bombers had used the main entrance to the base and had probably got hold of security passes. A third car, used in the getaway, was found burnt out in Belfast shortly after the bombs went off.
Thirty-one people were injured, including a soldier who received 60 percent burns.
The IRA, which wants a united Ireland, ended a 17-month ceasefire on February 9 with the first of a series of bombs on the British mainland. But it had not attacked Northern Ireland until this week.

The group denied that it was trying to draw its Protestant rivals into reviving Northern Ireland's 25-year civil war, saying it only wanted to stun Britain into allowing its political arm, Sinn Fein, into peace talks.
Sinn Fein has been banned from the talks sponsored by the British and Irish governments until the IRA calls a new truce and gives up its weapons.
Police said that the Lisburn attack had been planned since June, when the talks began.
